recipes.name: Vegetarian Corn Dog Casserole
ingredients_raw: 2 (8.5 ounce) packages dry corn bread mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a shallow 3 quart baking dish.
In a large skillet over medium heat, melt butter, then saute celery for 5 minutes. Stir in green onions, and saute an additional 5 minutes. Place in a large bowl and set aside.

Cut hot dogs lengthwise into quarters, then cut into thirds. In the same skillet, saute hot dogs for 5 minutes, until lightly browned. Mix hot dogs into celery and onions. Set aside 1 cup of this mixture.

In a medium bowl, combine eggs, milk, sage, pepper, and corn bread mix. Stir well to combine, then stir into remaining hot dog mixture. Mix in 1 1/2 cups cheese. Spread mixture into prepared baking dish. Top with reserved hot dog mixture and remaining 1/2 cup cheese.
Bake uncovered in preheated oven for 30 minutes, until golden brown.

raw_recipe.headline: Vegetarian Corn Dog Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Vegetarian hot dogs are baked with celery, onion, Cheddar and corn bread mix seasoned with sage and black pepper.

review.reviewBody: I came up with a recipe almost identical to this one about two weeks before I saw it. So I prepared this recipe to see how it stacked up against mine. It's very tasty, I like it. Try throwing in a can of no-beans chili and make it taste like a CHILI corn dog. Even better.

My speedy and simplified version was really good. No saute at all, just cut up Nathans hot dogs right out of the pkg, substitute onion powder for sliced onion. So all I really did was beat 2 eags, blk pepper and Jiffy corn bread mix (I did add the milk as directed on Jiffy mix), stir in hot dogs, cheese, and bake! 13yo son loves this served with Busch's vegetarian baked beans. Will try vegan version for my vegan daughter next.

Good recipe. I left out the celery and onion to make mine REALLY kid friendly (if making for grown-ups I'd definitely leave it in), and instead I added celery salt* and onion powder. Used a box of Jiffy corn bread mix and turkey hot dogs (watch the celery salt if you use regular hot dogs - might make it too salty) I halved the recipe and baked in an 8x8 pan for 20 mins - any longer would've been too much (next time I'll bake for 18mins). Be careful of the timing, especially if you omit the onion and celery, as they add moisture. I DID use the sage in this. I think that if you use light or vegetarian franks in this, it is a good idea to kick up the cornbread. If you use regular hot dogs, you may not need the sage...it's a matter of personal cornbread preference, I guess (I'm from the south and I like seasoned cornbread) Thanks for the recipe.

This was delicious! I used regular hotdogs because I had a bunch on hand. I cut the celery, onion and hot dogs using the food processor and omitted the sage since I didn't have any. I followed another persons suggestion and didn't reserve any of the hotdog mixture for the topping. I just mixed everything together and then topped it with a little extra cheese. This got rave reviews from my husband and my son. I am thinking the next time I have to bring a potluck dish, this will be it since it is pretty simple to make.

This turned out great! I did modify a few things though: Instead of green onion I used white and sauteed it with the celery (I reduced celery to 1.5 cups) I cut the hot dogs smaller as well as adding about a tablespoon of sugar while they were sauteeing which allowed a really nice caramelization as a result! In the "wet mix" (milk, eggs, etc.) I increased the milk to 1 2/3 (since so many comments said it was dry) I only used 1 tblspoon of sage and added some garlic powder and salt ..the only thing I will add/change when I make this again is to increase the topping of cheese to one cup! It was great!

I am only giving this 3 starts because I made a lot of changes to the recipe but it turned out really good. First, I omitted the celery and sage. My grocery store carries a mix of frozen onions red and yellow peppers. I sautéed that in a cast iron skillet. Then added a few chopped cherry tomatoes. Removed from the skillet then added the chopped hot dogs to the skillet and browned them. 1 1/2 cups of milk was way more than the 2 packages of corn bread mix called for so I followed the amount on the package. I took the suggestion of another reviewer and added a can of creamed corn. Then I cooked it in the hot cast iron skillet. Yum

Great recipe! I have used beef hot dogs or turkey dogs and this turned out great. I didn't use the sage or green onions but added a little onion salt and some precut frozen onions. I also cut out the celery because I don't like the taste but added a can of green chilis. It gave the casserole a nice kick and both my fiance and 20 month old loved it. It also tastes good with a little Franks hot sauce on top. Oh, and I did use more cheese than in the recipe but didn't put any on top until the last five minutes. And I only needed to cook mine about 20 minutes so I would watch it really closely after about 18 minutes.

I'm not much of a hot dog fan but this really good. I think the sage gives it a great flavor. I did make some changes though. I cut the hot dogs into smaller pieces and put 2 cups of cheese in it with a cup sprinkled over the top...kids love it that way. I put the cover on the last 5 minutes or so since I have had a problem with it getting too dark. By the way, the 15 ounce cornbread mix works fine with this recipe.

Very easy to make, and the kids loved it. But, I think the prep time is longer than 10 minutes -- closer to between 15 and 20, depending on how fast you chop. I mixed it all up the night before, though, so when I got home from work, all I had to do was pop it in the oven.

I work in a special ed class room of middle school students and they choose this recipe to make for a meal...they removed the celery, green onions, sage & pepper but added a can of whole corn and it was WONDERFUL. While they were making it I wasn't sure I would want to try any but I did and it was great!!!! Can't wait to make it for my family.

Made this last night with some semi-homemade chili beans & green salad on the side. It was a big hit with my husband and daughter. Will make it again. Went by the recipe, except I didn't have sage and used just a very small amount of poultry seasoning. I love mustard on my corn dog, so I used some mustard to dip my bites in before I ate them. Oops, forgot...used 1/4 pound hotdogs from Costco to make it, they are very good dogs.
I did the non vegetarian version, using regular hot dogs and I enjoyed the result very much. Easy recipe and a delicious result.

I had high hopes, but it was pretty dry. Loved the concept - maybe I'll play with it a bit to make it a little less dry and granular. The celery and green onions really added a great flavor! A work in progress

I will make this again bc it was pretty easy and fun for my girls to chop the veggies and hotdogs. However, next time I will not put the sage in there. I think that made it taste a bit like stuffing and I'm not a huge fan of that. Next time I think I will add some cumin or cardamom.
It was very dry and needed more flavor. I did add a little more milk as some suggested. We dipped each bite in a little mustard and catsup, which helped a bit.
Yes made few changes it's fantastic.

This tasted super good, but I put it in the wrong-sized dish so it cooked very unevenly. As result, I had to have it with ketchup, which tasted good with it. For some reason it was reminiscent of thanksgiving stuffing.
My kids (and I) LOVE this recipe!! It has become a staple recipe in my household.
awful
Not sure if this is kid friendly, but it is very tasty indeed. Something different for a change to the regular corn bread.
